chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Dancers fade away: Willie Green and the off-Broadway shows
summary: Green names Willie Green, who did 103 wings and went back to Indiana, and others who moved into Off-Broadway shows like Eddie Cantor's Banjo Eyes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Who were some of the dancers at this time?
That were trying to break through?
Well there -- the principal dancers at that time was --

Yeah -- what you call -- he was very excelling as a tap dancer -- they called him Willie Green, see, he could do 103 different wings. You know? And he used to exit doing military tap. See? Something about the services, the Army. And I mean he always got curtain calls, but he went away, went back to Indiana. And -- well you see something happened, I don't know -- I hope he didn't you know, I think he -- he still had a happy life, you know, but that place it took a lot out of the -- especially the tap dancers --

-- see it was black and white dancers, they was trying to change the place, the name of some of them, bring back the Hotcha, or something, you know -- no body was buying, you see and they didn't care whether they got the world tours and the monarchy, really or not. You see? See and they stopped, they said what're we knocking our heads up against it -- the writing is on the wall. You know.
